messages:
devon: Quick follow-up on the cache separation RFC — sketched a migration path that avoids touching the hot runtime token path. TL;DR: introduce a Cache Facade service, keep a tiny L1 in the runtime, move bulk prefix/KV to facade. Questions on SLOs and ownership below.

maria: can you paste the sketch and the failure modes?

devon: sure, rough sketch: 
- Cache Facade (stateless front, talks to redis-cluster backend)
- Runtime L1: 64MB LRU for micro-prefetch / token prefixes
- Protocol: simple HTTP/1 GET + JSON, small payloads (no streaming)
- Migration: dual-read mode -> validate hit ratio & latency -> cutover via flag

Example proto: 
```
GET /v1/cache/{key}
Headers: X-Client-Version: 1
Response: 200 {"value": "...", "ttl_ms": 120000}
503 on miss-backend error
```

Failure modes I see: network flaps adding p99, redis reshard causing spikes, stale TTLs if writeback async.

sam: main risk is tail-latency. If we add a remote hop p99 could blow past runtime SLO. How do we keep 99p tight?

anika: keep L1 for critical short prefixes and a circuit-breaker with adaptive bypass. If facade p99 > +20ms relative to baseline we short-circuit to runtime local cache. Also async prefetch for session continuation.

devon: planned mitigations: 
1) L1 local with strict size + eviction metrics
2) Synchronous read from facade but with very short client timeout (50ms) then fallback to runtime LRU
3) Canary traffic runs with full tracing so we can correlate p99 to model generation latency
4) Backpressure: degrade non-critical prefetches instead of blocking generation

maria: metrics to track in the rollout: p99/p95/p90 latency (end-to-end gen), cache hit ratio (facade + L1), eviction rate, facade CPU, network egress, errors and 5xxs, SLO breach count. Add tracing ids so we can slice by model & seq_len.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary started: cache-facade v0.1 -> staging (tag: feature/cache-facade) :rocket:

sam: perf harness — please include seq lengths {128,512,1024}, payload mixes (chat vs one-shot) and 1000tps baseline. I want 90/95/99 numbers for each. Also include cold-starts.

anika: abort strategy: if facade p99 delta > +20ms for 30m or error rate > 0.5% auto-roll back the feature flag. Also add a manual "bypass" header: `X-Cache-Bypass: true`.

devon: rollout proposal: 
- feature-flag behind config service
- internal canary (20% of internal org) 24h
- 10% prod for 48h with enhanced logging
- 50% for 72h
- 100% and deprecate old path after 2w stable
Auto rollback triggers on SLO breaches.

maria: timeline? This is in the long-term refactor bucket but ops wants dates for capacity planning.

devon: target end of Q2 for initial prod canary. Could accelerate if staging perf looks clean (2 weeks earlier).

sam: tech debt notes: we need gating tests in CI to assert no regressions on ordering and streaming. Also add a lint to prevent new code paths bypassing L1 unintentionally. I'll own the harness pieces.

anika: I'll draft the runbook for ops: failure scenarios, steps to bypass, how to repro p99 spikes locally, and query patterns to look for.

devon: ownership: infra will own facade ops (provisioning, SRE runbook), runtime team owns the L1 client and compatibility layer. We should add an interface contract doc (small OpenAPI + error codes).

maria: storage backend? ops asked about per-customer isolation vs single cluster.

devon: plan: single redis-cluster per-region with logical namespacing per-customer. TLS + at-rest encryption. We avoid per-customer clusters for cost but add strict RBAC + audit logging. If a customer requires isolations we can offer dedicated cluster as an enterprise option.

ops-bot: infra-bot: provisioning request created -> ticket #3218 (redis-cluster staging).

maria: one more: does this affect private deploys / on-prem? We need a small deployment doc making facade optional (local embedded redis or provided endpoint).

devon: yes, config-driven: `cache.mode: [embedded|facade|disabled]`. Default hosted uses facade. On-prem can use embedded redis or point to customer-managed cache.

sam: locking question: will this change token streaming ordering or KV semantics? streaming must stay identical.

devon: no change to streaming/generation contract. Runtime still owns the generator state machine. Cache is read-only for prefetched prefixes and does not mutate generation ordering. We will add an invariant test in integration suite.

maria: I'm merging notes to the RFC doc and adding migration steps + dashboards. Please add the sample feature-flag names and alert thresholds.

anika: I'll own runbook and the alert thresholds. devon/sam please add unit/integration tests and perf reports.

devon: thanks all. posting small TODOs: 
- sam: perf harness & CI gate
- anika: runbook + ops checklist
- maria: dashboards + RFC update
- devon: facade prototype + OpenAPI contract

maria: :+1: pushing this into the RFC PR. If anyone wants to propose a different backend (rocksdb object store) open a follow-up thread.

ops-bot: note: rolling canary will emit detailed traces to `infra-traces` project for next 48h.

devon: ok closing thread, will add protobuf + sample client snippets to the RFC. Thanks.
